2.measure_note: True LANDSCAPE page (/Rotate 90; poppler renders 2200 x 1700 at 200 dpi), so unlike the scanned archive sheets the rows advance NORMALLY top-to-bottom and the axis is y. rowbands detects the printed rules; the table's own grid is [13.76 top border, 16.94, 20.06, 23.29, 26.50, 29.68, 32.88, 36.06, 39.24, 42.44, 45.65, 48.82, 52.00, 55.18] on a constant ~3.19 pct pitch. TWO DETECTED RULES WERE DISCARDED AS ARTEFACTS: 31.41 and 32.18 are the COUNTY'S BLACK REDACTION BARS over the donor street addresses, not table rules - they sit inside a single band and break the otherwise exact pitch (29.68 + 3.19 = 32.87 = the detected 32.88). 11.24 is the rule under the page title, outside the table. Header row = [13.76,16.94]; row 1 is the grey shaded strip below it; the filer's seven entries are rows 2-8. Column bands from the vertical rules (6.30 / 13.86 / 44.57 / 83.80 / 93.75). MEASURED, then PROVED with a scratchpad raster crop rather than make_snippet: pages 2 and 3 of this PDF carry /Rotate 90, and scripts/campaign_finance/make_snippet.py maps pct->pixels with pdfinfo's UNROTATED MediaBox (612 x 792) while pdftoppm's -x/-y/-W/-H address the ROTATED raster, so its --value crop lands in the wrong cell on a rotated page. Verified: a make_snippet crop aimed at this page's row 2 amount returned the Address column of a different row. The bands below are in the frame the brief specifies - percentages of the page AS POPPLER RENDERS IT, rotation included - which is what rowbands measures and what a re-render reproduces; only the verification tool disagreed, and the shared script was left untouched.
